title: What is diabetes?
summary: Introduces diabetes, its common symptoms, prediabetes and type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and the role of exercise and diet.

atoms.title: 1 in 10 Americans live with diabetes
atoms.question: What does it mean to live with diabetes?
atoms.text: For the 1 in 10 Americans living with diabetes, it means managing blood sugar (glucose) levels. Glucose is the main source of energy for the body's cells, and insulin plays an important role in managing it. Whether newly diagnosed or living with diabetes for some time, careful diabetes management may make a world of difference.

atoms.title: Common symptoms of diabetes
atoms.question: What are the symptoms of diabetes?
atoms.text: Symptoms include feeling thirsty or hungry, peeing more often, feeling tired, itchy skin, dry mouth, unintended weight loss, blurry vision, frequent infections, cuts that heal slowly, breath that smells like acetone or nail polish remover (a sign of ketones rising to unsafe levels), nausea and abdominal pain. Call your doctor right away if you have these symptoms.
questions: What are early signs of diabetes?

atoms.title: Why diabetes symptoms need quick action
atoms.question: Why should diabetes symptoms be treated quickly?
atoms.text: Without medical intervention, a person with diabetes may suffer from damaged organs, lose consciousness and even slip into a life-threatening coma, also called diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Being able to act quickly may potentially save a person's life.

atoms.title: What prediabetes is
atoms.question: What is prediabetes?
atoms.text: Prediabetes is when your blood sugar levels are high, but not high enough to be considered diabetes. If prediabetes is left unchecked, it can turn into type 2 diabetes. There are positive steps you can take to get prediabetes under control.

atoms.title: What type 1 diabetes is
atoms.question: What is type 1 diabetes?
atoms.text: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune condition in which the body mistakenly attacks and destroys the cells in the pancreas that make insulin. It was once known as juvenile diabetes because most people diagnosed are in elementary school or are preteens. There is no way to prevent type 1 diabetes, and symptoms may appear quickly.

atoms.title: What type 2 diabetes is
atoms.question: What is type 2 diabetes?
atoms.text: Type 2 diabetes, the most common form of diabetes, is when your body does not use insulin properly. Some people are prediabetic before becoming diabetic. It used to be known as adult-onset diabetes, but today more kids are being diagnosed, possibly because of the rise in childhood obesity. No one knows exactly what causes diabetes, but there are known risk factors.
questions: What is the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes?

atoms.title: Exercise and diet in managing diabetes
atoms.question: Can exercise and diet help manage or prevent diabetes?
atoms.text: When it comes to managing, delaying or preventing diabetes, exercise and diet can both play a big role. These are two areas where you have ways to help control your health. UnitedHealthcare also offers guidance on coping with a new diabetes diagnosis and on controlling diabetes with exercise.
